content.text: : S. aureus, Proteus mirabilis, E. coli, Aspergillus (fungi)
: ⇡ moisture (swimming, humid), trauma (cleaning, Q-tips, hearing aids, earplugs), immunosuppression (HIV)
pain w/ ear canal traction (pulling up & back)
: avoid swimming, keep ears dry, avoid cotton swabs & scratching ear canal
: severe variant of acute otitis externa;
granulation tissue at cartilage-bone junction of EAC
⇢ bone erosion, soft tissue involvement, intracranial extension, abscess
Granulation tissue/ear drainage culture prior to initiating empiric ABX
: second-hand smoke, daycare, bottles/pacifiers, supine feeds
S. pneumoniae, H. flu, M. catarrhalis
▪︎ET in kids shorter, narrower, more horizontal ⇢ nasopharynx secretions more easily reflux into ET ⇢ more prone to AOM
▪︎inflammation of the mastoid air cells; MC in children <2yo
S. pneumoniae, H. flu, M. catarrhalis
: inflammation from acute purulent otitis media extends into the mastoid antrum & air cells in the temporal bone, resulting in fluid accumulation & bacterial infection
: begin days to weeks after onset of AOM
▪︎CT scan of temporal bone w/ contrast
: myringotomy & tympanostomy tube insertion to facilitate drainage
